source_row.rationale: While both ESR and CRP are nonspecific inflammatory markers, CRP tends to rise and fall more rapidly in response to acute inflammation (making it useful for tracking short-term changes in inflammatory activity or treatment response), while ESR tends to change more slowly and can remain elevated longer, reflecting some differences in their underlying biological mechanisms and clinical utility.
